data.navTitle: 气体牌、分子模型与原子卡
data.title: The balls that stand for water
data.goal: The balls that stand for water
data.situation:
On a low table, coloured balls represented atoms. Jo joined two hydrogen balls to one oxygen ball to build the model of a water molecule. The molecular model was much larger than any real molecule, and the guide asked visitors not to take its scale literally. Behind it, a board named gas as one state of matter. Separate cards identified oxygen and hydrogen gases, while an atomic diagram showed the structure of one atom. Maya kept the whole water model in one hand and an individual ball in the other. The two objects answered different questions about the same material. Jo: Is this ball a molecule?
Guide: Here it represents an atom. The joined group represents a molecule.
Maya: Are the colours real?
Guide: They help us distinguish the model parts; real atoms are not these painted balls.

readingBlocks.zh: 低桌上的彩色球代表原子。乔把两个氢球接到一个氧球上，拼出水分子模型。分子模型比真实分子大得多，讲解员提醒游客不要按模型比例想象实物。后面的板把气体列为物质状态之一。卡片分别标出氧气和氢气，原子图展示一个原子的结构。玛雅一手拿完整水模型，一手拿一个球；两者回答同一种物质的不同问题。

readingBlocks.en:
Jo: Is this ball a molecule?
Guide: Here it represents an atom. The joined group represents a molecule.
Maya: Are the colours real?
Guide: They help us distinguish the model parts; real atoms are not these painted balls.
readingBlocks.zh:
乔：这个球是分子吗？
讲解员：这里它代表原子，连接成组的球代表分子。
玛雅：这些颜色是真实的吗？
讲解员：颜色帮助区分模型部件，真实原子不是这些涂色球。

glossary.zh: 既非固体也非液体的一种物质状态；气体
glossary.note: 气体没有固定形状；a gas 指某一种气体。
glossary.example: The board named gas as a state of matter.
glossary.exampleZh: 展牌把气体列为物质状态。

externalEvidence.definition: a fluid in the gaseous state having neither independent shape nor volume and being able to expand indefinitely

glossary.zh: 氧气；模型标签也可指氧元素
glossary.note: 氧气；模型中的氧原子不表示水里含有游离氧气。
glossary.example: The board named oxygen as a gas.
glossary.exampleZh: 展牌把氧气列为一种气体。

externalEvidence.definition: a nonmetallic bivalent element that is normally a colorless odorless tasteless nonflammable diatomic gas; constitutes 21 percent of the atmosphere by volume; the most abundant element in the earth's crust

glossary.note: 氢元素；hydrogen gas 是氢气。
glossary.example: Two hydrogen balls joined the oxygen ball.

externalEvidence.definition: a nonmetallic univalent element that is normally a colorless and odorless highly flammable diatomic gas; the simplest and lightest and most abundant element in the universe

glossary.zh: 以化学键结合的一组原子所形成的分子
glossary.note: a water molecule：一个水分子。并非所有物质都有独立分子。
glossary.example: Jo built a model of a water molecule.

externalEvidence.definition: (physics and chemistry) the simplest structural unit of an element or compound

glossary.note: molecular structure：分子结构。旧词典例句对分子量的说明省略了质量，应理解为各原子相对质量之和。
glossary.example: The molecular model was much larger than a real molecule.
glossary.exampleZh: 分子模型远大于真实分子。

externalEvidence.definition: relating to or produced by or consisting of molecules

glossary.zh: 保有某元素化学性质的最小粒子；原子
glossary.note: an atom，复数 atoms；原子仍有内部结构。

externalEvidence.definition: (physics and chemistry) the smallest component of an element having the chemical properties of the element

glossary.note: atomic structure：原子结构；与 molecular structure 区分。
glossary.example: An atomic diagram showed one atom’s structure.
glossary.exampleZh: 原子图展示一个原子的结构。

externalEvidence.definition: of or relating to or comprising atoms
